notes: Sweden has no national duty rota and no regional duty-rota pages were found: night/weekend cover is organised by the chains (Evidensia, AniCura) and by Distriktsveterinärerna's county on-call, which is a phone standby service, not a published rota table. 11 entries count as 24 h after independent check on 2026-11-03: 8 staffed 24-h small-animal hospitals (Bagarmossen/Stockholm, SLU UDS/Uppsala, Malmö, Helsingborg, Strömsholm, Gammelstad/Luleå, Sundsvall, Östersund) and 3 Distriktsveterinärerna phone on-call entries (Gotland, Vimmerby, Västervik) whose pages state round-the-clock vet availability explicitly and list dogs/cats. Distriktsveterinärerna Öland (Färjestaden): page says a vet is reachable around the clock but does not state that small animals are covered, so it is listed as a clinic with emergency_24h false. Notably NOT 24 h despite assumptions: Göteborg (Evidensia Göteborgs Djursjukhus to 24:00, AniCura Västra to 21:00), Linköping (Valla to 23:00, Jägarvallen to 20:00), Kungens Kurva to 22:00, Växjö, Jönköping, Kalmar, Hässleholm, Karlstad, Örebro, Västerås, Gävle. Poison line: none. No animal poison line found; Giftinformationscentralen serves humans, and Agria's sjukvårdsrådgivning is included for Agria insurance customers (not stated to be open to the public), so it is not listed. Sites not usable: svf.se (bot check page), jordbruksverket.se/sva.se. Not used: PrivatVet / vetsverige / allaveterinarer / eniro (aggregators); Skellefteå and Umeå clinics only on PrivatVet. Left to research: Umeå and Skellefteå clinics via their own sites, other Distriktsveterinärerna county on-call pages (Norrbotten, Jämtland, Västerbotten, Skåne etc.), Uppsala district DV on-call, tourist-area clinics (Åre, Dalarna, Bohuslän coast), Sörmland, Kristianstad, Halmstad, Borås, Skövde, Trollhättan, and Stockholm night options outside Bagarmossen.
